summary: Add free-form tagging to alerts: a shared Tag entity in a many-to-many relationship with Alert, endpoints to add/remove tags, a tag query filter, and tags in AlertResponse.

acceptance_criteria.text: A Tag concept exists with a many-to-many relationship to Alert, backed by a new join table and EF migration.
POST /api/alerts/{id}/tags adds one or more tags, deduping case-insensitively, max 10 tags per alert, each tag 1-30 chars.
DELETE /api/alerts/{id}/tags/{tag} removes a tag assignment; returns 404 if the alert or the tag assignment does not exist.
GET /api/alerts accepts an optional tag query filter composable with isActive, severity, date range, and search.

planned_tests.test: Adding a tag to an alert persists a join row and the tag is returned on read.
The same tag name added to two alerts reuses a single Tag row.
POST with several tag names returns 200 with all tags on the alert.
Tag names differing only by case are deduped to one tag.
A tag longer than 30 chars or empty is rejected with 400.
A request that would push the alert above 10 tags is rejected with 400.
POST tags to a non-existent alert returns 404.
DELETE an assigned tag returns 204 and removes only that assignment.
DELETE a tag on a non-existent alert returns 404.
DELETE a tag not assigned to the alert returns 404.
DELETE matches the tag name case-insensitively.
GET with tag filter returns only alerts carrying that tag.
The tag filter composes with severity and isActive filters.
The tag filter matches case-insensitively.
AlertResponse includes the tag names for a tagged alert.
An alert with no tags returns an empty tags array, not null.
AddTagsAsync with a null request throws ArgumentNullException.
AddTagsAsync returns Success without persisting when all requested tags already exist.
AddTagsRequest DTO fails validation for an over-length or empty tag and for more than 10 tags.
RemoveTagAsync with an empty tag returns false without hitting the repository.
Service and controller forward the Tag filter to the repository/service.
AlertQueryRequest DTO fails validation when Tag exceeds the max length.
A single AddTagsAsync call mixing globally-existing and new names reuses the existing Tag rows and creates only the new one (batch-load path).

contract_changes.api: Add POST /api/alerts/{id}/tags and DELETE /api/alerts/{id}/tags/{tag}; add optional tag query param to GET /api/alerts; add tags array to AlertResponse.
contract_changes.database: New Tags table (unique Name index) and AlertTags join table via the AddTags migration.

boundaries.primary_slice: Alert tagging across controller, service, repository, EF model/migration, and DTOs.
out_of_scope: Tag listing, rename, or standalone tag management endpoints

assumptions: POST /api/alerts/{id}/tags accepts a JSON body { "tags": [...] } and returns 200 with the updated AlertResponse (404 if the alert is missing, 400 on validation failure).
DELETE /api/alerts/{id}/tags/{tag} returns 204 on success and treats the route tag value case-insensitively.
The tag query filter is a single, case-insensitive, exact-match value.
Tags are global shared entities: one Tag row per unique normalized name, enforced by a unique index and by application-level dedupe.
risks: Medium: new many-to-many plus Include changes the alert read query shape and adds a migration; rollback = revert the touched files and drop the AddTags migration.

Medium: the repository tests use the EF InMemory provider which does not enforce the unique Name index or case-insensitive collation, so dedupe and normalization must be enforced in application code, not only in the database.
scope_override_reason: Full-stack feature deliberately crossing Models, Common, Data contract, Data.SQL (config + migration), DTO, and API (service, mapping, controller) layers; 15 source and 3 test files is the minimum to satisfy all five acceptance criteria.
constraints: Tag length 1-30 chars and max 10 tags per alert must be enforced before persistence.
Tag dedupe and matching are case-insensitive.
Q1: stored/returned tag text normalization → lowercased
Q2: Tag row with no remaining assignments on delete → orphan cleanup (delete it)
Q3: max-10 applies to resulting total (existing + new); whole POST → 400 when it would exceed 10
